metadata.title: SEO landing pages built for real search intent
metadata.description: Build focused landing pages with clear intent, useful copy, internal links, strong technical defaults, and a practical review process.

hero.title: Build landing pages that answer real searches.
hero.summary: Turn useful search demand into focused pages people can understand, navigate, and act on.

problem.title: Scale makes weak pages easier to publish.
problem.introduction: A page template can save time, but it cannot create a reason to exist. These are the failures we prevent first.

items.title: Pages target the same intent
items.description: Several URLs compete for the same question because their purpose was never separated.

items.title: The copy changes names, not meaning
items.description: A repeated layout swaps a keyword while the examples, proof, and advice stay generic.

items.title: New pages sit on their own
items.description: The site publishes landing pages without useful internal links, navigation paths, or sitemap checks.

solution.title: Five rules for useful landing pages.
solution.introduction: The page system handles the repeated checks. The content still has to earn the URL.

items.title: Start with the question behind the search.
items.description: We decide what the visitor wants to learn or do before choosing a page type. Similar intents are combined instead of split across weak URLs.
highlights: Combine pages that would answer the same question

items.title: Put the page topic in the places that matter most.
items.description: The title, description, H1, and opening copy agree on the page's job. The first 200 words help a new reader understand it quickly.
highlights: Write a specific title and description
Answer the main question near the top

items.title: Share the quality checks, not filler copy.
items.description: Related landing pages can share composition and metadata rules. Examples, proof, objections, and links stay specific to each page.
highlights: Keep route content easy to review
Reject pages with no distinct value

items.title: Link pages where the reader needs them.
items.description: New landing pages receive links from relevant guides, product pages, and hubs. They also help visitors continue to the next useful answer.
highlights: Use anchor text that describes the destination
Keep every public page reachable in HTML

items.title: Measure usefulness after publishing.
items.description: We watch landing visits, meaningful actions, search queries, and page overlap. Weak pages are improved, combined, or removed.
highlights: Improve or remove pages that add no value

method.title: Publish in small, reviewable batches.
method.introduction: One strong page teaches more than fifty thin ones. Prove the content model before increasing volume.

steps.title: Group the demand
steps.description: Collect related searches and decide which ones need their own page.

steps.title: Write one complete page
steps.description: Answer the question with specific copy, proof, links, and a useful next step.

steps.title: Extract the repeated rules
steps.description: Keep stable composition and checks while leaving page meaning with the route.

steps.title: Publish, link, review
steps.description: Add sitemap and internal links, then watch queries, actions, and overlap.

outcomes.title: What a healthy page set gives you.

items.title: Clear search coverage
items.description: Each page owns a useful question instead of competing with a near-duplicate.

items.title: Consistent technical basics
items.description: Metadata, headings, canonicals, sitemap entries, and rendered links follow the same checks.

items.title: A smaller review burden
items.description: The team can check new pages in batches and remove weak ideas before they spread.

faq.title: Common questions.
faq.introduction: Short answers for teams deciding when a landing page deserves to exist.

items.question: How many landing pages should we publish?
items.answer: Start with the number you can make genuinely useful and review. Add more only when the search need, page purpose, and supporting content are distinct.

items.question: Can every keyword become its own page?
items.answer: No. Keywords that share the same intent usually belong on one stronger page. Separate them only when the visitor needs a meaningfully different answer.

items.question: Will these pages guarantee rankings?
items.answer: No. Good pages and technical defaults remove avoidable problems, but search performance also depends on demand, competition, authority, and how useful the content is.

items.question: Should landing pages live outside the navigation?
items.answer: They do not all need a main-navigation link, but every public page should have a useful path from relevant hubs or content and appear in the sitemap.

cta.title: Earn the first page before building the next fifty.
cta.description: Prove the intent, content, links, and conversion path on a real page. Then repeat only what makes the next page better.
cta.label: Review the launch priorities
